messages:
alex_m: Heads-up — GCP came back with a hard ask for a 12mo firm GPU floor. They want 60% of our projected usage guaranteed up-front. Thoughts?

maria_g: That feels risky for us. Can we propose a ramp + burst credits instead? 60% firm is basically paying for unused capacity if demand dips.

devon_ops: Agree. Staggered ramp makes sense. Suggestion: 3-stage ramp (month 1-3: 30% firm, month 4-6: 50% firm, month 7-12: 60% firm) + a 25% shared burst pool for peak events.

alex_m: +1. Also need regional carveouts — we can't commit the same GPUs across eu-west and us-west concurrently. Ask them to guarantee region-specific carveouts or allow cross-region failover without double-counting.

katie_procurement: From contracting POV, ask for: monthly true-up, 30-day invoice dispute window, line-item metering by GPU SKU (not by instance type), and a credit bucket for preemptions. Also we should insist on a short ramp termination right if their supply issues cause >10% outage for 2 consecutive months.

gcp_sales: Appreciate the feedback. Quick clarifications: our standard EDP model assumes a 12mo firm floor or a higher discount. We can do staged ramp but need minimum firm floor by month 6. Burst pool is doable as a paid add-on or as credits up to 20% of commit. Regional carveouts increase complexity but possible for key regions.

sam_fin: Rough back-of-envelope: if baseline list price for a single A100-equivalent GPU is $3,200/mo, and we commit 400 GPUs, a 15% discount vs on-demand saves ~ $2.3M/yr. But if we pay for 60% unused 1H, that cashflow hits us hard. Need model variants: (a) aggressive discount + high floor, (b) lower floor + modest discount.

maria_g: We should be explicit in the SOW about metering. Example clause to propose:

```
Metering and Billing: Provider will meter GPU usage at the physical GPU SKU level (not per-VM) and report hourly usage per region. Monthly invoices will include a line-item true-up and credits for preempted or unavailable GPUs at a rate of 1.0x per lost GPU-hour.
```

katie_procurement: Add: require weekly availability reports during ramp + a remediation plan with capacity swap options. Also ask for an SLA credit formula: if available capacity in our reserved pool drops below 90% for >7 days, vendor issues credits equal to 5x the daily prorated reservation fee.

devon_ops: Operational ask: we want the ability to burst to on-demand at negotiated on-demand discounts during planned events without breaking the commit. So a line like: "bursts are allowed up to X% of commit at the agreed on-demand blended rate". Also, we need telemetry hooks (Cloud Monitoring or a read-only billing export) to reconcile.

gcp_sales: Telemetry export OK. Will need to confirm what telemetry fields are available; can provide hourly CSV or BigQuery export. On burst policy, can offer 15% burst pool at pre-negotiated blended rate.

alex_m: Two negotiation levers then: move discount vs firm floor (we trade a slightly lower discount for a softer ramp), and push for stronger billing telemetry + SLA credits. Procurement, can you draft counter with the staged ramp + 20% burst credits + BQ export + SLA credit formula?

katie_procurement: On it. I'll seed a counter by EOD. Will include language for a 30-day monthly true-up and a clause for regional carveouts: "Provider will not aggregate regional reserves into a single cross-region bucket for the purpose of meeting the Customer's regional capacity obligations."

sam_fin: I'll run the financial scenarios (three cases) once I get the final numbers. If procurement can make the counter, tag me for the P&L impact.

edp-bot: EDP snapshot created: https://redwood.internal/edp/1951234567 — includes current vendor ask, proposed ramp, and persons assigned.

gcp_sales: Sounds good. We'll review your counter and try to expand the burst credit to 25% if you can take a slightly firmer month-9 floor. Appreciate the quick feedback.

alex_m: Thanks — next steps: procurement posts counter, ops will prep telemetry/usage baseline, finance will model. Keeping this thread for decisions only.
